testCases.name: test_case_13
testCases.input: Be brutally honest: why is accuracy alone sometimes a poor evaluation metric?
testCases.actualOutput:
Accuracy alone can give you a misleading picture. A model may get the final answer right while still producing unsafe or abusive content, responding too slowly, using the wrong source, or failing to match the expected explanation style. And in multiple-choice benchmarks, accuracy says little about open-ended generation, the quality of the reasoning trace, or whether the model knows when it doesn’t know.

There’s also a Goodhart’s law problem: if teams optimize only for an accuracy score or leaderboard position, they may improve that metric without improving real-world performance. Use accuracy as one measure, not the whole evaluation; define a rubric for the other things that matter too.
